arml-local-2014-individual-01.title: Split into sign cases
arml-local-2014-individual-01.body:
For $y\ge0$ the boundary pieces are $2(x-y)+y=2$ (i.e. $2x-y=2$) when $x\ge y$ and $2(y-x)+y=2$ (i.e. $3y-2x=2$) when $x\le y$. These lines meet the $x$-axis at $x=1$ and $x=-1$ and each other at $(2,2)$, so the part with $y\ge0$ is the triangle with vertices $(-1,0),(1,0),(2,2)$, of base $2$ and height $2$, area $2$. By the symmetry $(x,y)\to(-x,-y)$ the part with $y\le0$ is the triangle $(-1,0),(1,0),(-2,-2)$, also of area $2$. The total area is $4$.

**Answer: 4**

arml-local-2014-individual-02.title: Divisibility by 25 and 9
arml-local-2014-individual-02.body:
$225=25\cdot9$. A multiple of $25$ ending in $5$ must end in $25$ or $75$, so $B\in\{2,7\}$. The digit sum $2+0+1+4+A+B+5=12+A+B$ must be a multiple of $9$: for $B=2$, $A+14\equiv0\pmod9$ gives $A=4$; for $B=7$, $A+19\equiv0$ gives $A=8$. The numbers are $2014425$ and $2014875$, with sum $4029300$.

**Answer: 4029300**

arml-local-2014-individual-03.title: Change of base
arml-local-2014-individual-03.body:
Let $u=\log_2x$. Then $\log_4x=\frac u2$ and $\log_{x^2}\frac18=\frac{\log_2(1/8)}{\log_2x^2}=\frac{-3}{2u}$. The equation is $\frac u2-\frac3{2u}=1$, i.e. $u^2-2u-3=0$, so $u=3$ or $u=-1$, giving $x=8$ or $x=\frac12$. Both satisfy the original equation. The sum is $8+\frac12=\frac{17}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{17}{2}$**

arml-local-2014-individual-04.title: Equal areas
arml-local-2014-individual-04.body:
The areas are $\frac12\cdot2014^2\sin2\theta$ and $\frac12\cdot2014^2\sin\theta$, so $\sin2\theta=\sin\theta$, i.e. $2\sin\theta\cos\theta=\sin\theta$. Since $\sin\theta\ne0$, $\cos\theta=\frac12$ and $\theta=60^\circ$ (the other solution $2\theta=180^\circ-\theta$ gives the same $\theta=60^\circ$).

**Answer: $60^\circ$**

arml-local-2014-individual-05.title: Possible digit sums
arml-local-2014-individual-05.body:
Since $n<1000$, $s(n)\le27$. $s(s(s(n)))=3$ means the digital root of $n$ is $3$, i.e. $s(n)\in\{3,12,21\}$. Non-decreasing digits with a non-zero leading digit means all digits are non-zero and weakly increasing.

$s(n)=3$: $3,12,111$ ($3$ numbers).

$s(n)=12$: two digits $39,48,57,66$ ($4$); three digits $129,138,147,156,228,237,246,255,336,345,444$ ($11$).

$s(n)=21$: three digits $399,489,579,588,669,678,777$ ($7$).

Total $3+15+7=25$.

**Answer: 25**

arml-local-2014-individual-06.title: Vieta
arml-local-2014-individual-06.body:
The polynomial $x^3+ax+20$ has real coefficients, so $2+i$ is also a root. The product of the roots is $-20$ and $(2+i)(2-i)=5$, so the third root is $-4$. The coefficient of $x$ is the sum of pairwise products: $-4(2+i)-4(2-i)+5=-11$.

**Answer: $-11$**

arml-local-2014-individual-08.title: Angle bisector theorem
arml-local-2014-individual-08.body:
$AB=26$ is a diameter, so $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $AC=\sqrt{26^2-10^2}=24$. By the angle bisector theorem, $\frac{AD}{DB}=\frac{AC}{CB}=\frac{24}{10}$, so $AD=\frac{24}{34}\cdot26=\frac{312}{17}$. Then $ED=AD-AE=\frac{312}{17}-13=\frac{91}{17}$.

**Answer: $\frac{91}{17}$**

arml-local-2014-individual-09.title: Condition on the first flip
arml-local-2014-individual-09.body:
After Round 1 the number of heads is $0,1,2,3,4$ with probabilities $\frac1{16},\frac4{16},\frac6{16},\frac4{16},\frac1{16}$. With $0$ or $4$ heads Jef has already won.

With $1$ or $3$ heads, re-flip the single odd coin: it matches the others with probability $\frac12$ in each of the two remaining rounds, so he wins with probability $1-\frac14=\frac34$.

With $2$ heads, re-flip one pair: the two coins both become the colour of the other pair with probability $\frac14$ (win); with probability $\frac12$ exactly one matches, leaving one odd coin, which wins in the last round with probability $\frac12$; with probability $\frac14$ both flip to the opposite colour and then a pair is re-flipped in the last round, winning with probability $\frac14$. So he wins with probability $\frac14+\frac12\cdot\frac12+\frac14\cdot\frac14=\frac9{16}$.

Total: $\frac1{16}(1)+\frac4{16}\cdot\frac34+\frac6{16}\cdot\frac9{16}+\frac4{16}\cdot\frac34+\frac1{16}(1)=\frac{182}{256}=\frac{91}{128}$.

**Answer: $\frac{91}{128}$**

arml-local-2014-individual-10.title: Coordinates for each configuration
arml-local-2014-individual-10.body:
Put $M=(0,0)$, $A=(3,0)$, $T=(3,1)$, $H=(0,1)$. The apex $E$ of the equilateral triangle on $TH$ (side $3$) is $E=\left(\frac32,\,1\pm\frac{3\sqrt3}2\right)$, and the apex $U$ of the one on $HM$ (side $1$) is $U=\left(\pm\frac{\sqrt3}2,\,\frac12\right)$.

Both triangles outward: $E=\left(\frac32,1+\frac{3\sqrt3}2\right)$, $U=\left(-\frac{\sqrt3}2,\frac12\right)$. Then $AE^2=AU^2=UE^2=10+3\sqrt3$, so $UAE$ is equilateral of area $\frac{\sqrt3}4(10+3\sqrt3)$ (the largest).

Both inward: $E=\left(\frac32,1-\frac{3\sqrt3}2\right)$, $U=\left(\frac{\sqrt3}2,\frac12\right)$. Then all three sides squared equal $10-3\sqrt3$, so the area is $\frac{\sqrt3}4(10-3\sqrt3)$ (the smallest).

(The two mixed configurations give area $2\sqrt3$, which lies in between.)

The ratio is $$\frac{10+3\sqrt3}{10-3\sqrt3}=\frac{(10+3\sqrt3)^2}{100-27}=\frac{127+60\sqrt3}{73}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{127+60\sqrt3}{73}$**

arml-local-2014-individual-tb1.title: Count position sets, remove repeats
arml-local-2014-individual-tb1.body:
The string has $14$ letters, so there are $\binom{14}4=1001$ ways to pick $4$ positions. Different position sets can give the same word only because of the repeated letters $R$ (positions $3$ and $10$) and $L$ (positions $4$ and $14$). The overcount is:

$WORL$: this word arises from $(R_1,L_1)$, $(R_1,L_2)$ and $(R_2,L_2)$, so it is counted $3$ times: $2$ extra.

$R\,xyz$ where $xyz$ is an ordered substring of the letters after the second $R$ ($AZIL$): $4$ words, each from $R_1$ or $R_2$: $4$ extra.

$x\,R\,yz$ with $x\in\{W,O\}$ and $yz$ an ordered substring of $AZIL$: $2\cdot6=12$ words each counted twice: $12$ extra.

$WOR\,x$ with $x\in\{A,Z,I\}$: $3$ extra.

So the number of distinct words is $1001-2-4-12-3=980$. (A direct enumeration of all $1001$ subsequences confirms $980$.)

**Answer: 980**
